posts.name: scifantasy
posts.cooked:
Wow, am I the first to post? Well, so it goes.

The Eternal Haka, OG Bunker, and OG Ra against OG Baron Blade in Wagner Mars Base: Challenge Mode.

(Which means that even after you flip the Baron, if he gets 15 cards in his trash, game over.)

Minted this one by the skin of my teeth. Haka had 3 HP, Bunker had 1, and Ra was (ahem) toast. Tanking speed was the name of the game for me: I didn't wait to set up or get damage reduction or Ongoing destruction out, so at the end of the game Blade had both Basklash Fields, the Living Force Field, and even a Remote Turret out. Between Punish the Weak, Imbued Fire, the Staff of Ra, and Flame Barrier, I think Bunker actually ended up being the least damage-dealing party member. Though he also did lay the final smackdown when the numbers were getting close and I started worrying about getting double-tapped by the Backlash Fields. (Hid behind a Meteor Shower for a round or two to let the Maintenance Bot push Bunker into the safe zone, then dropped it for a multi-power Flak/Grenade combo turn that dropped Baron from 3 HP to 0. Yes, I needed both--Living Force Field.)

posts.name: Sonvar
posts.cooked: You don't choose the order.   It's based on the order they came into play.   If you played Ground Pound then Self-Destruct Sequence comes out during the environment turn at the start of Haka's turn Ground Pound is destroyed then you get the option about skipping your turn for Self-Destruct Sequence.  If Self-Destruct Sequence comes out then on Haka's turn you play Ground Pound on the following start of turn for Haka you have the option to skip the rest of your turn for Self-Destruct Sequence which if you chose yes makes the check on Ground Pound skipped.

Wow!  That was the answer for an easy Mint on this one.   Unless you have a villain or environment that destroys Ongoings or makes the heroes damage themselves, the Ground Pound/SDS combo is pretty unstoppable – Ground Pound prevents all non-hero cards (not just villain cards, or non-hero targets) from doing damage, so long as Ground Pound stays in play, the heroes are completely immune to outside damage.  Can anyone think of other cards/environments that Ground Pound would work with, i.e., cards that repeatedly ask the heroes to skip their turn, like SDS?   

 

SPOILER:

 

 

 

 

I had Haka do everything he could to draw cards (Mere, playing "haka" cards, using his base power) until he drew Ground Pound.  Once the Self-Destruct Sequence came out, Haka played Ground Pound and kept it in play for the next 5 turns, immunizing the heroes from damage while Bunker and Ra pounded on Baron Blade.  The Self-Destruct Sequence was aborted conveniently in time for Haka to finish off Blade with a Rampage (putting 4 extra cards under Savage Mana), followed by a 10-HP Savage Mana shot.   Just for fun, I replayed the same scenario (but with different random seeds) 5X, and was able to easily beat Blade every time by exploiting Ground Pound/SDS.

posts.name: bolnerap
posts.cooked:
I went in with the idea to hide so much stuff under Savage Mana that he would have a hard time meeting the alt win condition. Instead, this turned into abusing the environment while Haka and Bunker built up for massive damage. I burned Ra down to 8 before healing him up a bit with Staves. Staff + Flame Barrier meant that for a while, Ra was outdamaging Blade even with double Backlash. Then the DR came out and I decided it wasn't worth it anymore, and turtled with Ra too.

Mint with Haka at 19, Bunker at full, and Ra at 12.

This was yet another one shot that shows off how utterly abusable the Mars Base can be. (See also the Legacy / Tempest 3H game against Advanced Voss where it's quite easy to let Oxygen Leak do much of the work.)
